name: SIGMA - Explicit-Credential Sign-In Recorded (Windows Security 4648) [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/auth_win_explicit_cred_account_sweep.yml (issue #192). Buckets Security 4648 explicit-credential logons by the source host (host.name) and alerts when a single host uses >=6 distinct target accounts (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName cardinality) within a 5-minute window — a password-spray / account-sweep indicator. The Sigma file is the documented logic-of-record; this threshold rule adds the cardinality count that sigma_eval.py / the lucene conversion target cannot express. security-auditor review (#393): the original "from": "now-6m" (a flat +1-minute overlap over the 5-minute "interval") was mathematically incomplete, not just approximate — a real sliding 5-minute window is fully contained in a single 6-minute run window only when its start falls in a 1-minute band out of every 5 (containment probability 1/5 = 20% for an arbitrary-phase campaign). Corrected to "from": "now-10m" (lookback >= interval + the 5-minute detection window), which GUARANTEES full containment for any campaign phase. Cost: the effective counting window widens from 6 to 10 minutes (slightly more false-positive-prone at the same cardinality threshold; not retuned here) and duplicate-alert risk across overlapping runs is not independently verified against multiple real Kibana scheduled runs in this change.
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: IT help desk or password-reset tooling touching many accounts from one admin workstation.
Backup or scanning service accounts connecting to many targets with explicit credentials.
